"This is genuinely one of my top tips for everyone over 40"(Image: Doctoramirkhan/Instagram)

Dr Amir Khan is urging everyone over the age of 40 to buy one specific item that he claims "could literally save your life" and "prevent years of damage". Taking to Instagram, the NHS GP, who regularly appears on ITV shows like Lorraine and Good Morning Britain, shared "genuinely" one of his best "top tips".

He said: "If you're over the age of 40, I genuinely think one of the best things you can do at home is buy a blood pressure monitor. It could literally save your life." In your 40s, blood pressure becomes a significant health issue.

As you get older, your blood vessels tend to stiffen, leading to an increase in blood pressure. Since high blood pressure often doesn't show any clear symptoms, it's commonly referred to as a "silent killer". For home blood pressure readings, the general targets, according to Dr Amir Khan, are:

Explaining what exactly blood pressure is and why it is important to monitor, Dr Amir Khan told his followers: "It's the force of blood pushing against the insides of your arteries. So when your heart contracts or squeezes to pump blood around your body, that's the top number. That's why it's a bit higher. When it relaxes between beats, the pressure falls a little bit, and that is your bottom number, your diastolic blood pressure."

The doctor said it's so important to keep tabs on your blood pressure because high blood pressure rarely causes symptoms. Most people feel completely well, but over the years, it can quietly damage their blood vessels, increasing their risk of heart attack, stroke, kidney disease, eye disease, heart failure, and even dementia. "That's why lots of people call it the silent killer", he said.

"Now, the beauty is that it's easy to measure. And if it's high, we can do something about it through lifestyle changes, medication or often both," he added. To get an accurate reading, Dr Amir Khan advises sitting quietly for five minutes beforehand. He also urges people to avoid caffeine, smoking, and exercise for about 30 minutes before, if possible.

"Now, sit with your back supported, feet flat on the floor, legs uncrossed, and rest your arm on a table so the cuff is at the level of your heart," he said. "And remember, keep it on your bare skin, not over clothing. Keep still, don't talk while it's measuring. And then take two readings one minute apart.

"Do this morning and evening for seven days. Ignore the first reading and average the rest. That's the measurement we use in general practice. So you're taking two readings one minute apart, but it's the second reading you're most interested in. Think of the first one as a practice."

The health expert urges people to buy a home blood pressure machine (stock image)

At the end of the video, he said: "Remember, you may not feel high blood pressure, but you can find it and finding it early can prevent years of damage before symptoms even appear. My top tip, buy a home blood pressure machine."
